tasks.task: Write a logo design brief a designer can build from

items.when: When a client is about to hire a logo designer and needs the brief and the checks to judge drafts
Before the brief, to find who the brand is for, who it competes with and where it could stand out
When the client sets no limits, to fix firm rules that still leave the designer room
When the brief is agreed, to list the obvious ideas, one surprising move and small-size tests
When the brief asks the logo to say five things and it should carry one

tasks.task: Explore logo and wordmark directions

items.when: Before any sketch, to find the one idea, one feeling and one symbol the mark should carry
When the client needs several directions, from wordmarks to symbols, each with its reasons
When the name itself should be the logo, to get five letter-shape ideas and a pick
When you want one guided run from tight brief to mark plan to strength test
When a direction needs a vector draft that can be scaled and refined
When there are several ideas, to score each and get a keep or drop call
When the wordmark is set in a font and the letters are not doing any work

tasks.task: Review logo drafts against the brief

items.when: When drafts arrive from a designer and the client needs a fair review, not a gut reaction
When you need the brief's own checks to judge each draft against
When a draft looks good large, to test it in one colour and at small size
When the client wants something new and risks throwing away what people already recognise

tasks.task: Build a colour palette with roles and contrast pairs

items.when: When you need five to eight colours with roles, values and a contrast table people can apply
When the client shares designs they like, to turn them into colours and feel you can reuse
When the client names a feeling, to see colour, type and image choices that support it
When the feeling is agreed and you need a small palette with one job per colour
Before the palette is approved, to check each text and background pair and get the nearest pass

tasks.task: Choose a font pairing and type scale

items.when: When the type system needs fonts, sizes, weights and fallbacks written so anyone can apply them
When the client has no fonts, to compare three pairs with sizes and line spacing
When the brand lives mostly on screens, to pick pairs that read well at every size
When the type is set on a sample page, to check size, spacing and line length where it is read
When the type choice is about taste and nobody has asked what the reader needs

tasks.task: Write a full visual identity brief

items.when: When a new or refreshed business needs an identity and will hire someone to draw it
When the client cannot describe the look, to pin down tone and feel in four answers
When you need the fixed core, what may flex and a test for every place the brand appears
When the look is undecided, to compare three mood board directions and merge a pick
When the choices are made, to write firm rules for colour, type and grid
When the brief is drafted, to find where purpose, voice and look do not agree
When the direction follows a trend and says nothing true about this business

tasks.task: Set mood board directions for the client to choose from

items.when: When the brand is only an idea, to get name, position and mood directions narrowed to one
When you need three distinct mood boards with photo, type and colour choices
When a direction needs pictures, to try one idea as four different treatments
When you want to explore looks fast and then reuse the style the client chose
When the boards show people, to check for stereotypes and faces that all look alike

tasks.task: Audit every logo, colour and font in use

items.when: Before a brand book or refresh, to list every version in use and where the brand has drifted
When files are scattered across tools, to find the guides and decks that exist and the gaps
When the live site is the truth, to pull its real colours, fonts and spacing
When the brand shows up on site, emails, pack and ads, to score what each one says
When you have the materials side by side, to find where they drift from the brand

tasks.task: Write the brand guidelines book

items.when: When staff make their own versions and one document must settle it
When scattered logos, colours, fonts and templates must become one book others can follow
When the book needs firm rules, not soft advice, for colour, type and grid
When the rules are agreed and the client wants a printable guide
When the business has almost nothing written down and needs a first guide to react to
Before the colour pages are final, to confirm every pair shown is readable

tasks.task: Write logo use and clear-space rules

items.when: When the logo needs versions, clear space, minimum sizes, backgrounds and misuse examples
When the file formats and where each version is used must be listed
When the mark must work as a browser icon and you need the full set of sizes
When you set the minimum size, to test the mark small and in one colour first

tasks.task: Write a mascot or character design brief

items.when: When an illustrator needs personality, shapes, colours, turnarounds, expressions and poses
When the campaign goal must be tied to what the illustrator is asked to draw
When the client wants to see a quick set of characters drawn from their logo
When the character is a person, to check it avoids stereotypes

tasks.task: Write AI prompts to test a mascot idea

items.when: When the character brief exists and the prompts must follow its shapes and colours
When one mascot idea should be tried as four different treatments
When a prompt needs subject, light, style and a leave-out list for a named image tool
When brand colours and avoid rules must be held inside every prompt
When the character drifts between images, to turn each fault into a prompt line and a check

tasks.task: Brief a spot illustration set

items.when: When a site or app needs a matching set and the illustrator must be able to quote from the brief
When the set is for articles or pages, to plan where pictures belong and what each shows
Before the brief, to agree the tone and feel every piece must keep
When the planned set looks like stock art, to get three hand-made alternatives

tasks.task: Spec an icon set that looks like one family

items.when: When icons need a grid, stroke, corner and size rule before anyone draws them
When the list is drafted, to plan a small clear set and test that each icon reads
When you need vector drafts of the icons to test the rules

tasks.task: Brief a picture book, mural or other large illustration job

items.when: When an author or venue needs one brief an illustrator can quote and draw from
Before the brief, to find the one idea and feeling the artwork should carry
When the job has a campaign goal and several pieces to deliver

tasks.task: Turn the approved brand into design tokens

items.when: When colours, fonts and spacing are approved and developers need a tokens file, not a PDF
When the tokens also need component notes, responsive sizes and a developer handoff
When you want one run from brief to rules, checked colours and a developer spec
Before handoff, to check light and dark pairs built from the tokens

tasks.task: Run a first trade mark search on a name or logo

items.when: Before a new name or logo goes further, to log obvious clashes from the official search tools
When you have a name, to get similar marks and risk factors flagged for a lawyer
When there is a shortlist of names, to score each and get a keep, fix or drop call

tasks.task: Spec email signature, letterhead and business cards

items.when: When the book must include specs for signature, letterhead and cards
When the letterhead carries text and needs a grid, a short type list and white space
When the pieces are drafted, to check small type and spacing where they are read

tasks.task: List the templates the team needs

items.when: When everyone makes their own slides and the book must name the templates to build
Before the list, to see which decks and documents the team already uses
When the team will build and reuse the templates themselves and you must check what the tool allows

tasks.task: Plan a refresh that keeps recognition

items.when: Before any change, to see what is in use and what people already know the brand by
When the client says the brand feels dated, to name what works and what is off
When the reason for change is clear, to set what to keep, what to change and the rollout
When a rename is on the table, to score keep against rename before committing
When the new look has a date, to plan the message and steps for each stage

tasks.task: Write a one-file brand brief with voice and story

items.when: When the brand cannot say why it is different, to get several ways to stand apart
When the brief needs a one-page voice guide with word lists and before and after lines
When the brief needs the founding story told in a human way
When there is a tagline, to score it on ten tests and get sharper versions
When the brief lists many virtues and no single thing that sets the brand apart

tasks.task: Set photo and image style rules

items.when: When the photo style is open, to compare styles and pick a main one, a test one and one to avoid
When the style is chosen, to fix models, light and layout in one file
When a photographer needs the rules as a brief for a real shoot
When the rules cover people, to check who is shown and how

tasks.task: Plan how sub-brands and product marks relate

items.when: When there are several brands or ranges, to set how they relate and what each is called
When the business runs more than one store or range and needs a naming rule to compare

always.when: Before any work on a brand that already has a live site: colours, fonts and voice
Before any brief or brand book goes out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the brand has no position or audience agreed and the look has nothing to stand on
When the identity is set and flyers, social posts or signs must be laid out
When the identity must go onto a box, label or pouch with legal panels
When a product team needs the brand as tokens and components, not a PDF
When the brand needs names, taglines or voice written at length
When the team needs slide and document templates built from the brand

gaps: No library item reviews logo drafts against a written brief; only the kit prompt and a strength test exist
No library item writes a mascot or character brief with turnarounds, expressions and poses
No library item briefs picture book, mural or spot illustration work; only the kit skill covers it
No library item specs email signatures, letterheads or business cards
No library item writes logo clear-space, minimum size and misuse rules
No library item tests mood board or logo directions with real buyers before the client picks
No library item covers brand motion: logo animation and movement rules
No library item checks font licences or image rights before a brand book is published
No library item plans a brand pattern, graphic device or illustration style as a system
No tool guide covers Figma or Adobe Illustrator
